question.text: Consider the functions $f_{1}(x)=x, f_{2}(x)=2+\log _{e} x, x>0$. The graphs of the functions intersect.

options.text: once in $(0,1)$ and once in $\left(e, e^{2}\right)$

solution.text:
$\mathrm{f}_{1}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{f}_{2}(\mathrm{x})=2+\log _{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{x}$
Let $g(x)=f_{2}(x)-f_{1}(x)=2+\log _{e} x-x$
$g\left(o^{+}\right)     < 0, g(1)>0, g(e)>0, g\left(e^{2}\right) < 0$
and value of $g(x)$ for all $x \geq e^{2}$ is negative.
$\therefore \mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})=0$ has two roots in $(0,1)$ and $\left(\mathrm{e}, \mathrm{e}^{2}\right)$
